div.p: Real-time task now emerges in various reliable systems; however, most existing schedulers of real-time tasks are limited to fixed priority scheduling. A dynamic priority scheduling model is derived for the preemptive earliest deadline first scheduling of periodic real-time tasks in the realtime reliable system. Moreover, a heuristic algorithm is present for the schedulability test, which is effective when the priority inheritance protocol is considered to prevent priority inversion.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: In some reliable system, such as power plants, hospitals, or manufacturing and transportation systems, a computation task is considered to be correct if it finishes within a specified deadline moment, otherwise it will cause disastrous consequences. The correctness depends not only on the accuracy calculation of the logic, but also depends on the complete time [1]. In this sense, all time-constrained computer applications require a real-time computer system. Scheduling algorithms and schedulability test for real-time tasks are the heart of real-time system. A scheduling algorithm is considered feasible when each task could be completed within the deadline.

In a single processor, preemptive real-time operating environment, there has been some very mature algorithm for the hard periodic task, including the monotonous rate algorithm (know as RM) [2], [3] and earliest deadline first algorithm (know as EDF) [2], [4]. RM algorithm is the optimal fixed-priority scheduling algorithm, according to the release period of task, the shorter the period, the higher the priority, then the first run. As long as the total load of periodic tasks is less than

(n is the number of periodic task, when the n is increased, the value is nearly equal 0.693) [2], the RM algorithm is feasible. EDF algorithm is the optimal dynamic priority scheduling algorithm, in accordance with the deadline of task, the more recent deadline, the higher the priority, and then the first run. EDF scheduling algorithm can guarantee all tasks to be completed within the deadline, as long as the total load of periodic tasks is more than one [2].

Another important aspect of real-time scheduling algorithms is the priority inversion [5]. When the two realtime tasks try to access a shared data, in order to maintain the consistency of the data, access must be in serial. If the lower priority task gains access first, then higher priority task request to access the shared data, then this high-priority task will be blocked until the low priority task completes this access. Now if there exits a third task, and its priority is between high and low priority, and it does not access the share data, so this task will seize the low-priority task, and indirectly blocked the high-priority task, and this blocking is uncertain. This is the priority inversion problem. The solution of priority inversion problems is the priority inheritance protocol (know as PIP) [6]: When a task blocks one or more high-priority task, the original priority of the task will be ignored, and the highest priority of all the tasks blocked by it, as its priority in the operation of critical access. When it leaves the critical area, the task goes back to its original priority. The priority inheritance protocol will avoid a lower priority task indirectly blocking high-priority task, but because there are still a higher priority task being directly blocked by lower-priority tasks, so the longest blocking time will be considered in the schedulability test. Now the scheduling algorithm commonly used by realtime systems, such as VxWorks and uc/OS-II, is fixedpriority scheduling algorithm. High-priority tasks always occupy low-priority tasks operation. However, unlike RM algorithm, the priority of a task is specified by the user, rather than by the period of the task, It is the guarantee that the user can always think it is important to give higher priority to the task, even if the task in time is not very urgent, and the shortcomings is reducing the total load of the system. They also adopt the priority inheritance protocol, but in the schedulability test, to calculate the load of a task, simply add the longest blocking time of the task [7], this has also led to lower the system total load for period real-time tasks. For the above-mentioned shortcomings, this paper will put forward a dynamic priority scheduling model for adopting EDF scheduling algorithm in a real-time embedded system, and by analyzing the maximum stealing time [8], [9] of EDF scheduling algorithm, give a more realistic algorithm of the schedulability test when the priority inheritance protocol is considered to prevent priority inversion.

div.head: II. THE DYNAMIC SCHEDULING MODEL
div.p: Because the EDF scheduling algorithm always choose the most recent task to run, so it needs to include the release time and the deadline time in each process control block (know as PCB) of system. Also in accordance with the order of each deadline, from nearest to farthest, arrange all ready PCB in a chain. According to priority inheritance protocol, it also need to record the current process occupying an exclusive lock and the current processes blocked by an exclusive lock in each lock object in system. The blocked processes also are arranged in a chain from nearest deadline to farthest deadline. The schedule function is always letting the first process in PCB ready chain run. When a case is as follows, the above chains might change; lead to switch the current running process:

• When a new process is released, the action: according to the deadline of the new process, add the new PCB to the ready chain; choose the first process in ready chain to run. • When a process is over, the action: removes the process from the ready chain; choose the first process in ready chain to run. • When a process locks success, the action: set the process as the current occupation process of the lock object.

• When a process is blocked, the action: remove it from the ready chain, then add it to the block chain of the lock object; according to the deadline of the first process in the block chain, adjust the order of the current occupation process of the lock object in the ready chain; choose the first process in ready chain to run. • When a process leaves the exclusion resource, the action: according to itself deadline, adjust its order in the ready chain; remove the first process in the block chain of the lock object, add it to the ready chain, and set it as the current occupation process of the lock object; choose the first process in ready chain to run.

div.head: B. The method of schedulability test with priority inheritance protocol
div.p: Theorem 2: If the total load of periodic tasks is not more than one, EDF algorithm can success scheduling all tasks, with the priority inheritance protocol, As long as
The B i represents the max running time of task i in all exclusive area, the f p represent the maximum stealing time.

Proof: When a process has succeeded occupying an exclusive lock, it will enter the exclusive area. In this period time, when some higher priority processes requests to occupy the same exclusive lock, they would be blocked; the maximum blocking time of the higher processes is just the max running time of the lower priority process in the exclusive area. Assume B represents this blocking time, this block by the lower process result in that all the processes whose priority is not larger than the highest priority of the blocked tasks postpone time B, except the lower process itself. Considering the blocking time as the stealing time mention above, as long as B < f p , it is ok. When the task leaves the exclusive area, the stealing time ends, and the highest priority process will run, and the maximum stealing time is change to (f p -B). It is important that when this lower process finish, the maximum stealing time will comeback to f p , because this total running time is not changed. That is to say the same task only can block the other higher processes once affecting the maximum stealing time. That is to say each task only can be blocked once by each other. Therefore as long as

div.head: IV. CONCLUSION
div.p: This article puts forward a design of dynamic real-time scheduling algorithm in embedded real-time system, implementing the EDF scheduling algorithm and priority inheritance protocol. it also brings up a more effective schedulability test for sharing some exclusive resources among multiple real-time tasks. This design and the schedulability test improve the total load of real-time system. There are still some problems, one is calculating the maximum stealing time. Though we can get the all free time distributing in a hyper period, but the method is a recurrence process, spending much time. In fact we only need the last free time, which is maximum stealing time. Finding a direct formula to calculate the maximum stealing time is a meaning work after this article. The other is the time switching between processes, when considering the process switching time, the running time C i and blocked time B i of each task must be added by the switch time respectively.
